title: A pull request merged without a single comment from a reviewer it explicitly requested
author: off-by-one
description: Compares a repository's merged pull requests against its own inline review-comment history, reading a field none of the sixty-two prior recipes ever reads: a pull request's own requested_reviewers list. GitHub's own structured solicitation names a login whose review was explicitly wanted before the work landed, but nothing forces that request to be answered before merge, and nothing retroactively flags an unanswered one once the PR merges. When a merged PR names a requested reviewer and ListReviewCommentsInARepository's own read never carries a single comment from that login on this PR, the solicitation and the outcome have quietly drifted apart with nothing on GitHub's side that would ever compare them again.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long the pull request has sat merged while its named requested reviewer's own review comment never appears, not flat. Under 24 hours since merge scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- a requested review may simply still be in flight). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal: an exact login match failure between a merged PR's own requested_reviewers list and every review comment's own author on record for that PR number. The 24h window matches merged-pr-branch-not-deleted's and deleted-branch-pr-still-open's own bar for a structurally similar family -- a GitHub-native, post-resolution expectation nothing forces closed, only a human notices -- reused here rather than inventing a new number. A pull request that has not merged (still open, or closed without merging) is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- no resolved promise exists yet to check a review against. A merged pull request naming no requested reviewer at all is excluded too -- no solicitation was ever made. A merged pull request with no recorded merged_at is excluded as malformed, not guessed into either bucket. A blank requested-reviewer entry (an empty string) is excluded outright -- not a real login. A requested reviewer who left at least one review comment on the PR, at any point in the read-so-far history, fulfilled the request -- excluded, named not hidden, the ordinary case.
